facts.text: Shelby Park began in 1847 when German working‑class settlers first populated the area bounded by Kentucky, Preston, Bergman, and Logan Streets.
In 1908, the 17‑acre Shelby Park was established at the neighborhood’s center, later becoming a civic gathering spot.
The park’s layout was designed by the renowned Olmsted Firm, the same architects behind many U.S. national parks.
A Carnegie‑endowed library opened in 1911 on Oak Street; its Second Renaissance Revival style was crafted by Arthur Loomis.
The Jefferson County Public School system once wanted to build a school on the park, but the neighborhood association saved the space as the heart of Shelby Park.
Shelby Park was named for Kentucky’s first governor, Isaac Shelby, whose legacy dates back to the state’s founding.
